generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The original code in three of the four tests used `.watcher-history*` (no hyphen before the wildcard), while the helper now uses `.watcher-history-*`. This is a behavioral change for those tests. In practice both patterns match the same data-stream backing indices, so this is almost certainly fine, but it is worth confirming that no other index (e.g., a legacy alias) could match `.watcher-history*` but not `.watcher-history-*` in the test environment.

The comment states the method "throws an AssertionError" if the data stream is not ready, but the method itself does not throw an `AssertionError`—it delegates to `ensureGreen`, which may or may not throw one depending on the test framework's implementation. The Javadoc also says it "Returns a SearchRequestBuilder containing up to the default number of watch history records (10)," which conflates the request builder with the eventual search response. A clearer description would be something like: *"Ensures the watcher history data stream is green, flushes and refreshes it, and returns a `SearchRequestBuilder` targeting `.watcher-history-*`."*

The original code in three tests called only `refresh(...)`, while the helper calls `flushAndRefresh(...)`. This is a stricter (and generally more correct) operation, so it should not cause regressions, but it is a subtle behavioral change worth noting in the commit message.

review_comment: `.setSize(...)` drops out here (and a few other places) -- is that okay?

Some places only needed the count (so size=0 was fine), and some wanted the single record (so size=1 was fine). Since we always expect either 0 or 1 documents in this index it didn't seem to cause any problems to just use the default size. Worst case, we pull back a single history document that we don't care about that gets immediately garbage collected. It avoided passing an argument into this method that might just add confusion.
